candidate.signature: (finite ordered list of D1 bits)->(minimal-order nonnegative integer, ordered list of binary taps a1..aL)
candidate.behavior: For a finite GF(2) word s_0..s_(n-1), find the least L in [0,n] for which there exist a_1..a_L in {0,1} satisfying s_t = XOR_(j=1..L) a_j*s_(t-j), simultaneously for all observed t=L..n-1. Among all admissible tap lists for the minimal L choose the lexicographically smallest list (a1 foremost, 0<1). Return (L,taps). The empty word and any all-zero word return (0,[]). This describes only the observed finite word; it does not assert correct unseen future symbols, cryptographic strength, real SDR synchronization or physical hardware behavior.

positive_witnesses.source: Sage 20-symbol LFSR example, with tap convention fixed by this D10 proposal

falsifiers: Claim that 010101 has order 1 merely because its visible primitive full-repeat root is 01; the first symbol 0 and second 1 cannot follow a degree-1 GF2 homogeneous recurrence.
Treat the input 1 as an L=0 recurrence; order zero forces all observed bits to zero.
Return a longer L when a shorter recurrence fits all observed positions.
Return lexicographically larger taps when two minimal-order recurrences both fit the observed finite word.
Claim the inferred finite recurrence predicts arbitrary unseen future bits or certifies SDR non-noisy clock lock.
Claim Sage berlekamp_massey returned taps are always identical without reversing the polynomial and applying the declared lexical tie rule.
